answer: Each node’s EigenTrust centrality is computed from normalized, reciprocity-weighted trust paths, while exponential decay with a fixed temporal half-life steadily discounts stale service. A new identity—even one named copper, karst, or zenith—starts with negligible incoming trust, near-zero eigenvector centrality, and no credible transitive support. It therefore cannot pass consensus by multiplying identities; influence requires sustained, reciprocated honest service over time.
